Recommendation: do not buy local AI hardware as the default path; use hosted models for most workloads, with a narrow exception for sensitive or latency-critical cases where a controlled on-prem deployment is justified.

Hosted models are faster to start, easier to scale, and usually cheaper at low to moderate volume. They remove the need to procure GPUs, manage drivers, patch inference stacks, monitor utilization, and plan refresh cycles. For product teams, that means fewer moving parts and more time spent on application logic rather than infrastructure. The main tradeoffs are data residency, cost at high sustained volume, and dependence on an external provider. Those are real concerns, but they are not reasons to buy hardware for every team.
